instruction: Identify the month with the lowest total cost for 2020 and make its name bold in column A.

metadata.explanation: Task requires finding the minimum total monthly cost in 2020 (which is 349 in March at row 22, cell I22) and applying bold formatting to the month name cell (A22). The evaluator extracts both cell formatting and data from the spreadsheet, dynamically identifies the row with the minimum 2020 cost, and verifies: (1) the correct month was identified (50% score), and (2) that month's name cell in column A has bold formatting applied (50% score).

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies both requirements: (1) finding the month with lowest 2020 cost, (2) checking bold formatting on that month's name cell
Getter now dynamically identifies the 2020 column by searching the header row for '2020' (calc.py:66-73), resolving the previous hardcoding issue
Metric logic is correct: finds minimum cost row (lines 32-39), compares with expected row (lines 44-57), and checks formatting (lines 59-86)
Partial credit scoring is semantically sound: 50% for correct month identification, 50% for correct formatting
Data flow is correct: getter extracts right state -> metric compares right aspects -> expected value is correct (A22, bold=true for March)
